messages:
tyler: heads up — seeing a NaN spike on staging after the kernel-selector change that prefers an fp8 fused kernel for short-prefix paths. repro on model redwood/gptx-7b-quant, batch=1, seq=1024
maria: ugh. any stack traces or a tiny repro? can you paste logs + profiler timeline?
tyler: quick logs pasted below:
```
2026-03-10T14:23:01Z WARN kernel_selector: chosen=fp8_fused_qkv idx=3
2026-03-10T14:23:01Z ERROR runtime: forward produced NaN at layer 24 matmul
2026-03-10T14:23:01Z INFO calib: using scale=0.03125 smoothquant_enabled=true
```
kevin: did we run the new calibration sweep before rolling selector? maybe some layers got extremely small scales. also note we changed the batching heuristic last deploy (long-prefix grouping) which alters sequence length distribution.
maria: can you attach a tiny nvprof / nsight timeline? memory transient + kernel timing help debug underflow/overflow races.
tyler: pasted a condensed nvprof excerpt:
```
GPU kernel: matmul_fp8_fused      2.1ms
GPU kernel: scale_clip           0.03ms
GPU kernel: matmul_int8         1.9ms
GPU transient memory delta: +120MiB before layer24 -> freed after layer24
cudaMemcpy: 0.4ms
```
sophie: @tyler can you dump per-layer quant scales and the smoothquant alpha used for this run? if one layer's scale collapsed we could be hitting FP8 exponent underflow or denorm behavior.
danny: tagging infra-bot to kick off a full profile capture across a failing trace so we have metrics and traces for the incident.
infra-bot: collect:profile started job id=pf_4123 path=/tmp/profile_pf_4123 (ETA ~40s)
tyler: scales from the failing run: layer22:0.03125, layer23:0.03125, layer24:0.015625, layer25:0.0625. alpha for smoothquant=0.5
maria: layer24 scale 0.015625 — that's low. FP8 has limited exponent range; with aggressive smoothquant alpha we might be shrinking per-channel scales too far and causing underflow to zero or denorms that later produce Inf/NaN during fused matmul.
kevin: we saw a similar signal when swapping to the fused kernel last month — the fused path lacks the older numeric-clip guard we had in the int8 path. two levers: add a clip in the fp8 path or fallback to int8 for small scales.
sophie: quick experiment idea: policy that picks kernel per-layer by scale threshold, e.g. if scale < 0.02 -> prefer int8 kernel; else fp8. we already have a kernel selector flag prototype: --min-scale-fallback=0.02
tyler: running a gated deployment in staging with that flag now. will post results.
... (40s) ...
tyler: quick result: enabling --min-scale-fallback=0.02 removed the NaN in 10/10 repro runs. Perf diff is small on overall latency because only handful of layers fall back.
maria: nice. any observable quality delta? fallback to int8 might change logits slightly.
tyler: checked a small prompt set: token-level KL between fp8-all and mixed-fallback ~ 0.0009 on average. quality looks fine for these cases.
kevin: we should add a temporary probe in the selector to sample a few requests with both kernels (A/B) and log scale->error correlation, then remove once calibration sweep is tuned. also add a perf counter to detect sudden increases in transient memory — that + low scale seems correlated.
danny: filing a small incident PR to hold rollout: infra/rollout #PR-1892 and runtime/patch #PR-1893 that adds the guard and test that reproduces scale collapse.
sophie: long-term: revisit smoothquant alpha sweep and add per-channel min-scale floor during calibration phase; also add a numeric sanity test in the model onboarding pipeline to run a short fp8 stress test.
tyler: created PRs and added a unit test that runs 50 short sequences to ensure no NaN. i'll keep the staging flag on until we push a calibration fix. thanks all. :thumbsup:
